title: Dichotomy.

artist_statement.text:
Dichotomy.


A single line runs through this frame and decides everything. On one side, rows of palm trees stand in ordered silence inside a jail facility, green and geometric, tended and contained. On the other, a residential neighbourhood sprawls freely in concrete and colour, unplanned and ungoverned.


From above, the irony collapses into a single image. The place with no freedom looks like a garden. The place with freedom looks like a cage of a different kind. Inside that green order, movement is timed, monitored, and permitted by the state. Outside it, movement is free but formless.


Shot in my hometown, this aerial photograph asks what custody truly looks like when the architecture of confinement is indistinguishable from order, and the architecture of freedom is indistinguishable from chaos. The line between them is the only honest thing in the frame.

This is dichotomy. 


Shot on DJI Mavic Pro drone at 26mm,

 f/2.2, ISO 100, 1/120 secs. Processed in Photoshop. 2952 x 3888 pixels.


Location: Rajahmundry, India. 

Year: 2017.


“I, Rakesh Pulapa, declare that if this piece is selected and purchased by the 6529 Network Museum, this work will be released under CC0 and I have full rights to make that release.”
